metadata.title: IgG1 Analysis Tools: AlphaFold Y-Shape Studio for screening AlphaFold 3 antibody models
metadata.description:
AlphaFold Y-Shape Studio 1.3.0 is a desktop application for screening AlphaFold 3 IgG1 antibody models and inspecting their structures with Matplotlib. It assigns chains and domains, measures hinge and Fab/Fc geometry, reports candidate disulfide bonds, and provides an interactive three-dimensional preview. Analysis runs locally.

Changes in version 1.3.0

  • Matplotlib/Tk is the only viewer; OpenGL code and dependencies have been removed.
  • Revised interface with light and dark themes, progress, cancellation, stable model selection, keyboard controls, camera reset, and PNG/SVG/PDF export.
  • Corrected Fc descriptors to use a molecule-relative axis, making them invariant to rigid rotation. Thresholds are unchanged; Fc values can differ from version 1.2.0.
  • Separate output folders for each completed run, preserved previous results.
  • Corrected Linux environment selection and a Windows executable built from the same versioned source.

Downloads

  • Windows: AlphaFold_Y_Shape_Studio_Windows_x86_64_v1.3.0.zip contains the ready-to-run executable and its bundled runtime. Extract the entire ZIP and keep the _internal folder beside the executable. Python installation is not required. The executable is unsigned; do not disable operating-system security protections.
  • Linux and source: AlphaFold_Y_Shape_Studio_Source_v1.3.0.tar.gz contains the source, pinned requirements, installer/launchers, regression tests, and build instructions. The tested configuration uses Python 3.10 with Tk and venv. Run bash install_and_run.sh from the extracted folder; the first installation requires internet access.
  • Both archives include the complete 15-model sample dataset, documentation, dependency notices, and the upstream MDAnalysis source archive.

Validation and limitations

Software testing covers Windows 11 x64 and Ubuntu 22.04 under WSL2/WSLg, including 75 regression tests on each platform, the bundled Windows executable, geometric invariance, malformed inputs, output preservation, profile comparisons, and interface/export behaviour. The supplied IgG1 sample produces 15 analyzed structures, 3 passing models. See README.md for tested configurations and limitations.

This software is a geometric screening tool for AlphaFold3 output, not experimental validation of structure, function, or biological activity.

hits.title: IgG1 Analysis Tools: AlphaFold Y-Shape Studio for screening AlphaFold 3 antibody models

metadata.title: Structural Covariance Network Analysis in EPM1: An R-Based Graph-Theoretical and Permutation Testing Pipeline
metadata.description:
This software provides a reproducible R workflow for whole-brain structural covariance network (SCN) analysis in progressive myoclonus epilepsy type 1 (EPM1; Unverricht–Lundborg disease) and healthy controls. Regional brain volumes are normalized to total intracranial volume and residualized for age and sex. Group-level weighted structural covariance networks are then constructed from Pearson correlations between regional measures, retaining positive correlations at a fixed threshold of r ≥ 0.30.

The pipeline calculates global network density, global efficiency, transitivity, modularity, average path length, and nodal efficiency. Group differences are evaluated using 5,000 label permutations, with false discovery rate correction applied to nodal comparisons. The script also exports the patient-minus-control edge-difference matrix and derives leave-one-out (jackknife) subject contribution measures for global network metrics and a predefined nodal metric, enabling subsequent association analyses with clinical variables.

The workflow uses interactive input-file and output-directory selection and therefore contains no hard-coded data paths. Participant-level imaging and clinical data are not included.

Keywords: EPM1; Unverricht–Lundborg disease; progressive myoclonus epilepsy; structural covariance network; structural MRI; graph theory; network neuroscience; nodal efficiency; permutation testing; R.

hits.title: Structural Covariance Network Analysis in EPM1: An R-Based Graph-Theoretical and Permutation Testing Pipeline

metadata.title: Reproducibility package for "Multi-timescale PTM architecture in human RNA polymerase II"
metadata.description: Human RNA polymerase II (Pol II) carries an extensive landscape of post-translational modifications (PTMs) and conformational states that collectively coordinate transcription and co-transcriptional RNA processing. Here, we compile residue-level annotations across the twelve human Pol II subunits and formulate an explicit discrete-state framework for the C-terminal domain, the non-CTD region of Rpb1, and subunits Rpb2–Rpb12. Under an independent-site construction, the curated residue-state landscape has a maximum logarithmic state-space size of 707.98 bits per Pol II molecule, including 211.22 bits contributed by the CTD. Experimental human CTD mass-spectrometry data support the five canonical phosphoacceptor-position classes represented in the framework and show qualitative agreement between the predominant Ser5-P and Ser2-P classes and the largest modeled position-class contributions. Empirical kinetic observations further support a multi-timescale architecture spanning seconds to hours. The quantitative framework distinguishes model-defined state-space size from physiological entropy and provides a reproducible approach to PTM-rich regulatory systems.
metadata.notes: If you use this reproducibility package, please cite both the archived software/data package and the associated manuscript.

metadata.title: monetary-topology: mechanism models for a topological framework of claims and resources
metadata.description: Small mechanism models for a framework in which a monetary claim and the resource it points at are distinct objects. Each model isolates one mechanism, exposes fewer than a dozen parameters, and reports a criterion that can fail. Seven carriers, each a separate regulatory environment, have produced measured non-zero readings on real transaction data, each against a floor that is measured rather than asserted. Every criterion is in the record at the same resolution, whichever way it came out, including the ones this programme superseded on its own evidence.

metadata.title: QQA4CO: Quasi-Quantum Annealing for Combinatorial Optimization
metadata.description:
QQA 0.9.0 — Typed primal-dual runtime

QQA 0.9.0 promotes QQA4CO from a primal-search toolkit to a typed, auditable primal-dual and hybrid optimisation runtime while preserving the existing research APIs.

Highlights

  • Stable solve, plan, and inspect contracts backed by machine-readable model/factor capabilities, strict finite bounds, and tri-state feasibility.
  • Robust normalized QQA dynamics, heterogeneous replicas, tempering exchange, factor preconditioning, historical archives, adaptive augmented Lagrangians, and archive-centred restarts.
  • Device-resident typed factor operations, GPU repair/local search, bounded autotuning, and roofline telemetry.
  • Sparse PDHG, dual crossover, SCIP feedback, general QUBO persistency, isolated exact workers, CP-SAT scheduling, and SAT/MaxSAT runtimes.
  • Benders, column generation, progressive hedging, spatial branch-and-bound, DRO/scenario/SAA tools, black-box acquisition, and OOD-gated learned planning.
  • Pickle-free atomic checkpoints, checksum-protected result packages, bounded schema-only service jobs, Model Doctor, Optimization Cockpit, Decision Explorer, and domain templates.
  • Refreshed documentation and a credential-free typed primal-dual notebook covering diagnosis, events, visualization, resume, and package verification.

Validation

  • CI passed on CPython 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14.
  • The built-in correctness sweep passed 29/29 checks, including exact -N energies for periodic ferromagnetic Ising instances through N=64.
  • Secret scan, strict documentation build/deploy, full-source type checking, package build, Twine metadata checks, archive portability scans, and the performance gate passed.

See the 0.9.0 changelog and next-generation runtime guide for details.

metadata.title: Explainable AI-Driven Multi-Horizon ROP Forecasting for Risk-Aware Drilling Decision Support
metadata.description:
This repository contains the reproducibility code associated with the manuscript “Explainable AI-Driven Multi-Horizon ROP Forecasting for Risk-Aware Drilling Decision Support.”

The archive includes the data preprocessing pipeline, baseline implementations, RMC-Transformer training code, repeated-run experiments, statistical analysis, risk-parameter sensitivity analysis, and the external validation workflow on the public Volve/USROP benchmark.

The public USROP dataset used for external validation is available at:
https://github.com/AndrzejTunkiel/USROP
and is described in:
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.petrol.2020.108069
The original Volve field data are available from Equinor at:
https://www.equinor.com/energy/volve-data-sharing

The Oman-6ROP dataset is not included in this repository. It is derived from proprietary industrial drilling data and cannot be publicly redistributed because of intellectual-property ownership, confidentiality, privacy, contractual, and data-use restrictions. Access, if considered, remains subject to permission from the industrial data owner and the applicable confidentiality and data-use agreements.

The repository therefore provides the complete software workflow and configuration files, while the restricted Oman industrial data must be supplied separately by authorized users.

metadata.title: Probabilistic representation learning of baseline transcriptomes enables prediction and pathway-level interpretation of anticancer drug responses
metadata.description:
This repository contains the code, data, trained models, and analysis outputs associated with the manuscript “[Insert manuscript title]”, submitted to Scientific Reports.

The repository provides computational materials for reproducing the main analyses of a representation learning-based framework for anticancer drug response prediction and pathway-level interpretation. The workflow includes predictive performance evaluation, identification of shared and drug-preferential latent factors, KEGG pathway enrichment analysis, QAL333 validation, comparison with reference anticancer drugs, and zebrafish xenograft response analysis.

The repository is organized into four main directories:

- code/: analysis scripts and notebooks for predictive modeling, latent factor analysis, pathway enrichment, QAL333 validation, and zebrafish response analysis.
- data/: input data used for the analyses.
- models/: trained models and preprocessing objects used for latent representation extraction.
- results/: output files generated from the analysis workflow, including prediction results, latent factor results, pathway enrichment outputs, QAL333 projection results, and zebrafish analysis results.

For pathway-level interpretation, latent factor-associated gene lists were generated by ranking genes according to the absolute Spearman correlation between baseline gene expression and latent scores across training cell lines. The top 100 genes for each selected latent factor were used for KEGG pathway enrichment analysis, and significantly enriched pathways were mapped to predefined functional groups.

The README file provides details on the repository structure, software environment, analysis workflow, data availability, code availability, license, and citation information.

hits.title: Probabilistic representation learning of baseline transcriptomes enables prediction and pathway-level interpretation of anticancer drug responses

metadata.title: Icepack model and configuration files for local AIM simulations
metadata.description:
These files comprise the unique software used to simulate local field tests of sea ice thickening via artificial flooding in Cambridge Bay, Nunavut, CA and at Vallunden Lagoon on the island of Svalbard between 2024 and 2025. The files are as follows:

  • Icepack.zip-- a compressed directory containing the Icepack (v1.4.1) model used for simulations, including all relevant code changes. 
  • *_icepack_in-- namelist files configuring each set of simulations for each field location. CB is for Cambridge Bay, SV is for Svalbard. 
  • *_hosing.dat-- the manually created flooding files used to provide the rate of seawater pumping that occurred at each experiment location.
  • *_atm_MDF.nc-- the atmospheric forcing files used to drive sea ice simulations with Icepack at each site
  • *_ocn_MDF.nc-- the oceanic forcing files for each site (only used if ocn_data_type == 'MDF' in icepack in (ocn_data_type == 'default' was used for published results).
